annotator_prompt.name: final_layout_keyframe
annotator_prompt.description: After the first requested container was lifted, returned and released, the robot obscured the next requested container in the front view while that container was outside the wrist view. The stored target_locations correctly identified it, and completed_lifts correctly selected it, but the policy estimated an inaccurate approach position and yaw. This breaks SUFFICIENCY: a silhouette-centre identity does not preserve the hidden top-face geometry. Add a field holding the last demonstration frame showing the settled final arrangement with the requested containers unobstructed. Set it at the video cycle and retain it unchanged throughout execution. It preserves geometry for still-unmoved targets, not the current geometry of returned containers. Example value: V113.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: final_layout_keyframe
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: When approaching a later requested container after returning the first, the robot can obscure the target in the front camera while it lies outside the wrist camera. The identity list and completion count remain correct, but they cannot supply its hidden grasp geometry, breaking SUFFICIENCY. During the video cycle, select the last shown frame of the settled final arrangement in which the requested containers are unobstructed, and write its label as final_layout_keyframe, for example V113. Carry that label unchanged at every act cycle. Do not replace it with a robot-occluded execution frame or update it when a completed container is returned.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action: The failures occurred when the open hand had withdrawn after returning the first requested container and was approaching the second. The identity list and completion count selected the correct target, but the predicted horizontal approach positions were wrong: the target could be clipped in the wrist view, occluded in the front view, or outside the wrist view altogether. These are geometry-related SUFFICIENCY failures, not evidence for changing target identities or completion transitions. Extend the existing calibrated reconstruction rule as follows. For an unfinished, unmoved target, use final_layout_keyframe as an unobstructed reference whenever current views hide or truncate its physical top corners. Match the reference container using target_locations; do not treat that stored silhouette centre as its grasp-axis projection. Fit the horizontal square top and visible vertical sides using the calibrated reference front view together with any usable current observations. Recover height from consistent geometric evidence rather than choosing an arbitrary projection plane. In a clipped view, use visible physical edges and their square constraints to infer missing corners; the image boundary is not an object edge, and the centroid of the visible fragment is not the grasp centre. If the current wrist view provides no usable target geometry, do not force a wrist-based estimate: use the unobstructed reference geometry for the stationary target. Average reconstructed physical top corners for x,y and infer yaw from reconstructed world-plane edges. Use this centre for the open approach at z=0.20 m, then refine from current calibrated views before closing at z=0.0633 m. Do not use the final demonstration geometry as the current pose of a container that has since been moved. Keep the existing lift, return, withdrawal and completion rules unchanged. The additional inaccurate second-target approach for which no missing information was reported supports applying this same geometry rule consistently; it does not justify a separate memory field or a target-specific waypoint.

fields.name: target_locations
fields.description: During the video cycle, identify which container descends over each requested cube colour. Follow those containers continuously across the shuffle frames, including exchanges between identical-looking containers. Write their final front-image silhouette centres as [u,v] pixel pairs in requested colour order. Do not infer identity from the final arrangement alone or assume a container returned to its original identity because the arrangement repeats. Carry this list unchanged at every act cycle. e.g. [[131,71],[117,146]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of [u,v] front-image container-centre locations, in pixels, at the end of the demonstration, one for each requested cube colour in instruction order. Identify the container that originally covered each requested cube and follow its continuous motion through every shuffle; record its final location, not the cube's original location. Include no distractors. Use the centre of the entire visible container silhouette consistently. Set this list at the video cycle and retain it throughout execution, including after a selected container moves. e.g. [[131,71],[117,146]]

fields.name: completed_lifts
fields.description: Initialize to zero at the video cycle. Increment once when this cycle's motion frames show the next requested container rising with the closed gripper from grasp height to approximately 0.20 m TCP height. The container must move with the hand; a newly exposed cube supports confirmation. Count the observed lift, not a lift you are about to command. Do not increment for a static elevated grasp, a downward return, an open-hand withdrawal, or a grasp closure at low height. If the motion executes no steps, retain the count. Otherwise retain the incoming value unless this successful new lift is observed. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of requested containers already lifted successfully in instruction order. Initialize to zero at the video cycle. Increment at the first act cycle showing the selected container carried upward from grasp height to approximately 0.20 m TCP height with the gripper closed. Do not increment for closing at grasp height, returning a container, withdrawing with an open gripper, or continuing to hold an already-counted container. Retain the count otherwise. e.g. 1

texts.action:
At the video cycle output memory only. Execution starts with an open hand above the scene and completed_lifts equal to zero. Use target_locations to identify the requested containers in the current front image; the list records identities by their final demonstration locations, not their initial cube locations. Distinguish container identity from grasp geometry. target_locations stores whole-silhouette image centres for identifying containers, not projections of their grasp axes at a known height. Identify the selected container using target_locations, then locate its physical top-face corners using usable calibrated observations. For an unfinished target that has not moved since the demonstration, use final_layout_keyframe as an unobstructed reference whenever current views hide or truncate its physical top corners. Match the reference container using target_locations, without treating the stored silhouette centre as a grasp-axis projection. Use the current wrist view to refine that same container, not to switch to a nearby one. If the target is outside the wrist view or supplies no usable wrist geometry, use its stationary reference geometry rather than forcing a wrist-based estimate. In clipped views, infer missing physical corners from visible physical edges and square constraints; neither the image boundary nor the centroid of the visible fragment defines the container geometry. Recover the horizontal top-plane height from consistent container geometry and calibrated observations; where necessary, jointly fit a horizontal square top and vertical side faces to the reference front view and any usable current observations. Do not use demonstration geometry as the current pose of a container that has subsequently moved. Do not choose an arbitrary plane height or project the silhouette centre onto the table. For world-to-camera calibration R,t, the camera centre is C=-R^T t and the world ray through pixel [u,v] is d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1]. Its intersection with a top plane of height h is C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Reconstruct the physical top corners on this plane and average their world coordinates to obtain the grasp-axis x,y centre. Determine yaw from reconstructed square edges, not raw image-edge angles. Use this recovered x,y for both the open approach at z=0.20 m and the closing descent at z=0.0633 m, refining it with current imagery before descent. Robot-left is +y, which appears on the right of the front image. Grasp the container, not the cube.

Apply the following rules to the observed state, accounting for a lift observed in this cycle before selecting the action. With an empty open hand and an unfinished target, select target_locations[completed_lifts]. If not already above that container at approximately z=0.20 m, move to its world centre at z=0.20 m with the gripper open. Point straight down, roll=3.1416 and pitch=0, and align yaw with the container's opposing square sides. Infer the container centre independently of the reported TCP: long motions can stop roughly a centimetre short.

With the open hand above the selected container at approximately z=0.20 m, descend to the independently reconstructed grasp-axis centre at z=0.0633 m and close the gripper. Refine that centre from the current calibrated wrist and front imagery using the top-face reconstruction above. A small approach-motion error does not require another approach waypoint: correct x,y during descent. Neither the reported TCP x,y nor an assumed-height projection of the whole-silhouette centre substitutes for the reconstructed target centre. With the closed fingers around the container at this low height, raise its centre vertically to z=0.20 m, maintaining yaw and keeping the gripper closed. Fingers separated approximately 0.018 m each and a container between them indicate a grasp; do not release at this stage.

When a successful lift has just been observed and another requested target remains, return the held container before approaching the next one: keep the current TCP x,y and orientation, lower to z=0.070 m, and open at arrival. When the hand is open at this low return height, withdraw vertically at the current x,y to approximately z=0.147 m, remaining open. With the open hand at this withdrawal height, approach the next target at z=0.20 m. Do not regrasp the returned container merely because it is beneath the hand. completed_lifts distinguishes that completed target from the next requested one.

When the last requested container is grasped, lift it to z=0.20 m with the gripper closed; no return or extra container is required. If another cycle occurs after all requested lifts are confirmed, keep holding and wait briefly for termination.

For an unmatched or uncertain state, preserve the stored identities and completion count. Use the current wrist and front views to recover alignment. If empty and too low for safe lateral travel, withdraw vertically with the gripper open before approaching the unfinished target. If a grasp visibly failed, reopen while moving at least 5 mm, then realign and retry the same target without incrementing completed_lifts. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint; use a wait when only observation is needed.
